unit.title: Perform gas tungsten arc welding process to AWS specification (Pipe)

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A piping specification says small-bore process lines are to be GTAW welded "to the AWS code the Centre uses". A welder holds only a GTAW plate qualification. What is right?
options: He may weld the pipe, since a plate test covers every pipe size
He needs a pipe test that covers the sizes and positions
He may weld it if a pipe welder checks it afterwards
He may weld only the cap passes on the pipe

questions.stem: Why does a GTAW test on small-bore pipe generally cover larger pipe, while a test on large pipe does not cover very small pipe?
options: Large pipe is always made of a harder grade of steel
Small pipe is welded with a larger tungsten and cup
Large pipe tests are never bent or X-rayed
On a tight curve the position changes faster

questions.stem: Kemar's 6G test used GTAW for the root and second pass and MMAW for the fill and cap. What does his WPQ record for each process?
options: The thickness of weld metal each process laid
Only the process used for the cap
Only the make of each welding machine
The total time taken for the whole test

questions.stem: What is a consumable insert in a GTAW pipe root?
options: A soluble paper plug that holds the purge gas inside
A ceramic ring that stays behind the root
A ring of filler metal set in the root and fused in
A spacer wire pulled out before welding

questions.stem: Why might a WPS for a critical small-bore line call for consumable inserts in the root?
options: They let the root be welded with no argon
They make the pipe wall thicker at the joint
They give an even, smooth root profile inside
They remove the need for any fit-up checks

questions.stem: Before a socket weld is made, the pipe is pushed into the socket and then pulled back about 1.5 mm. Why?
options: So expansion cannot crack the weld
To make room for slag to fall into the socket
To let purge gas flow round the pipe end
To make the fillet weld smaller and quicker

questions.stem: On a 5G GTAW root, the second half must join onto the first half at the bottom and the top. How are the ends of the first half prepared?
options: Left as they are, with the crater open
Built up high, so the join has more metal
Hammered flat with a chipping hammer
Ground to a taper so the arc fuses through

questions.stem: Why is too much root penetration a bigger problem in small-bore pipe than in large pipe?
options: It makes the pipe wall much thinner at the joint
It narrows the bore and can block the flow
It makes the pipe impossible to paint
It stops the joint from being X-rayed

questions.stem: Which GTAW pipe root normally needs a back purge with argon?
options: Carbon steel water pipe
Galvanised fence post
Carbon steel handrail tube for a hotel
Stainless steel process pipe

questions.stem: On a humid morning in Port Antonio, droplets of water form on a cold pipe that is to be GTAW welded. What should the welder do?
options: Weld at once, as the arc will dry it
Warm the joint gently to drive off the moisture
Wipe the pipe with an oily rag so the water runs off
Spray it with water so it is evenly wet

questions.stem: A GTAW repair is needed on a water line in a hotel plant room. What must be done first?
options: Isolate, drain and dry the line, with a permit
Weld it with the water still flowing, to keep it cool
Turn the pressure up to find the leak
Wrap the pipe in wet sacks and weld

questions.stem: On a large-bore pipe joint, two welders GTAW weld at the same time on opposite sides. What is the main benefit?
options: It uses less argon in total
Neither welder then needs to be qualified for pipe
Heat goes in evenly, so the joint stays in line
It needs no tack welds at all

questions.stem: Why do welders mark their ID number beside each pipe weld they make on a job?
options: So each weld can be traced to its welder
So the pipe can be sold for more money
So the inspector knows where to cut it
So the paint shop knows the pipe size

questions.stem: A job uses an orbital GTAW machine that travels round the tube by itself. Who must be qualified to run it?
options: Nobody, because the machine does all the welding
Only the person who sold the machine
A welding operator, qualified on that machine
Any welder with an MMAW plate test

questions.stem: Why must tube ends for orbital GTAW be cut square and faced smooth?
options: So the tube is easier to paint afterwards
The machine cannot correct a poor fit-up
So the weld can be made with no argon
So the tube ends look neat in photos

questions.stem: A pipe joint is GTAW welded while turning rolls rotate it under a fixed torch. What is the AWS position?
options: 2G
5G
6G
1G

questions.stem: On a 2G GTAW pipe joint (pipe upright), how are the fill and cap usually laid?
options: One wide weave across the joint, from top to bottom
Stringer beads stacked from the bottom up
One bead in the middle, then the top
Beads laid only down the vertical sides

questions.stem: On a 5G GTAW root, the root inside the pipe is sunk in at the bottom (6 o'clock). Which change helps most?
options: Hold a longer arc at the bottom
Travel faster round the bottom

questions.stem: How are the tacks on a small-bore pipe GTAW root usually finished before the root is run?
options: Left full height, to hold the joint
Painted, to show where they are
Ground thin and tapered at both ends
Removed fully before the root starts

questions.stem: Which filler is a common choice for a GTAW root on carbon steel pipe?
options: ER70S-2

questions.stem: A welder must stop part way round a GTAW pipe root to get a new rod. How should he stop?
options: Break the arc at once and pull the torch away
Dip the tungsten into the pool to put the arc out
Leave the pool open and let it cool
Use the downslope and keep the gas on the crater

questions.stem: Which tool checks that the inside walls of two small-bore pipes line up at the joint?
options: A hi-lo gauge
A fillet gauge
A feeler gauge
A flowmeter

questions.stem: Thin-wall stainless tube about 1.5 mm thick is to be GTAW butt welded. How are the ends usually prepared?
options: Bevelled to 37.5° with a 3 mm root gap
Flared out with a hammer to fit
Square cut and butted tight, no bevel
Overlapped by about 10 mm and fused

questions.stem: A pipe is 60.3 mm across the outside. About how long is one pass round it? (Circumference = π × diameter.)
options: About 120 mm
About 190 mm
About 240 mm

questions.stem: A GTAW root on a 168 mm pipe is about 530 mm round. It is welded at 60 mm per minute. About how long is the arc time?
options: About 3 minutes
About 6 minutes
About 9 minutes
About 12 minutes

questions.stem: Each welder completes 6 small-bore GTAW joints a day. Three welders work on a line with 75 joints. How many full working days are needed?
options: 4 days
5 days
6 days

questions.stem: A pipe job has 40 welds. Which record links each weld number to its welder, WPS and test result?
options: The supplier's delivery note
The client's purchase order
The steel mill certificate

questions.stem: Why must a 6G pipe test stand be bolted or clamped firmly before welding starts?
options: So the coupon cannot move or fall in the test
So the stand does not need to be earthed
So the welder can lean on the pipe
So one person can move the stand round the bay

questions.stem: A welder steadies a pipe with his bare hand while starting the arc with high frequency (HF). What can happen?
options: He may get a sharp HF shock or a small burn

The argon will stop flowing

questions.stem: Why is a fixed-position pipe test coupon marked at the top (12 o'clock) before it is taken out of the stand?
options: So it can be stood the right way up to cool
So the welder's name can be written there
So the paint shop knows which side is outside
So strips can be taken from the right places round it

questions.stem: A pipe root shows a short length of incomplete penetration. Who decides whether it can be accepted?
options: The welder who made the weld
The inspector, using the code's limits
The next welder on the line
The storekeeper who issued the rod

questions.stem: A radiograph shows lack of fusion in a GTAW pipe root. How is it put right?
options: Run a second cap over the top of it
Leave it, because the cap is sound
Grind it out, re-weld and re-test it
Fill the spot from outside with filler

questions.stem: You plan the GTAW welding of a pipe skid with 30 joints. Which task should come before any welding starts?
options: Order the paint for the finished skid
Book the truck to deliver the skid
Write the final report for the client

questions.stem: Why is a welded pipe usually pressure tested with water, and not with compressed air?
options: Water is cheaper to buy than air
Air would rust the inside of the pipe
Water stores far less energy if the pipe bursts
Water shows up the welder's ID marks

questions.stem: Why should a pipe joint with only the thin GTAW root done not be lifted or moved?
options: The thin root can crack under the strain
The tungsten in the torch will go out of shape
The argon will leak out of the pipe
The tacks will become too hard

questions.stem: On a 5G joint, the root gap at one side is much wider than the WPS allows. What should the welder do?
options: Fill it with extra rod and carry on
Re-fit the joint so the gap meets the WPS
Weld much faster at the wide side
Pack the gap with a short piece of rod

questions.stem: A pipe weighs 5.44 kg per metre. About what does a 6 m length weigh?
options: About 22 kg
About 33 kg
About 54 kg
About 65 kg

questions.stem: Each GTAW pipe joint uses about 0.12 kg of filler. How much filler is needed for 40 joints, plus 10% spare?
options: About 5.3 kg
About 4.8 kg
About 4.4 kg
About 12 kg

questions.stem: A GTAW pipe root shows a line of unfused edge along one side of the joint only. What is the most likely cause?
options: The argon was too pure
The pipe was too clean
The torch and heat favoured the other side
The tungsten was ground too sharp

questions.stem: Why is a stainless steel pipe joint tacked only after the back purge is on?
options: The purge makes the tacks stronger than the root
The purge holds the pipes in line
The purge cools the tacks so they do not shrink
Tacks oxidise inside too, so they need the purge

questions.stem: On a job, 120 GTAW pipe welds are X-rayed and 6 are rejected. What is the reject rate?
The client's inspector wants to watch the first production weld. A welder starts before the inspector arrives. What should the team leader do?
options: Let him finish and show the inspector photos
Say nothing to the inspector about it
Tell the welder to finish quickly
Stop the work and wait for the inspector

questions.stem: A welder's GTAW pipe WPQ shows a "diameter range qualified". Where does that range come from?
options: The welder's own choice on the day
The code's tables for the size tested
The pipe supplier's catalogue
The size of the welding booth

questions.stem: Why are the open ends of welded pipe spools capped or covered before they are stored outside?
options: To stop the outside of the pipe rusting
To keep the paint on the spool dry
To keep dirt, water and pests out of the bore
To stop the spools rolling off the rack

questions.stem: A GTAW pipe test coupon fails visual inspection. Is it still cut for bend tests?
options: Yes, the bend test has the final say
No: a coupon that fails visual has failed
Yes, but only for the root bend

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A test coupon is made from two pieces of pipe, each 125 mm long. Ignoring saw cuts, how many coupons can be made from a 6 m length?
What is the name for the person qualified to run an automatic or orbital welding machine, as opposed to a manual welder?
What is the name for a joint where one pipe is fitted onto the side of another pipe, so that they form a T?
A line has 60 GTAW joints, and 10% of them must be X-rayed. How many joints are X-rayed?
Name the part of a GTAW torch that the shielding gas flows out of, which comes in numbered sizes.
What is the name of the point in an inspection plan where work must stop until the inspector has checked it?
What is the term for joining the end of one weld run into an earlier run, as at the top of a 5G root?
Each pipe joint needs 3 rods of 1 m for the root and 7 for the fill and cap. How many rods are needed for 12 joints?
What one word is used for the inside diameter of a pipe?
What kind of stamp, with rounded characters, is used to mark a welder's number on pressure pipe without cutting sharp notches?
In the filler class ER70S-2, what property of the weld metal does the number 70 give?
What is the name of the pipe drawing that shows a run in 3-D, with each weld numbered?
Four tacks are placed at equal spaces round a pipe joint. How many degrees apart are they?
What is the name of the wheeled stand that turns a pipe under a fixed torch for 1G welding?
Which element, added to tungsten as an oxide, gives the "ceriated" type of tungsten its name?

essays.stem: Describe how you would fit up, tack and GTAW weld a carbon steel pipe test coupon in the 6G position to a WPS, from the root to the cap.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the WPS for the bevel, root face, gap, filler, tungsten, current and gas. I clean the bevels and 25 mm inside and out to bright metal, set the root face, and line the pipes up with an even gap and no step inside, checked with a hi-lo gauge. I tack in three or four places, grind each tack thin and taper the ends. I fix the coupon at 45° in the stand, mark the top, and do not move it. I start the root just past the bottom and weld up one side to just past the top, then weld the other side, grinding the starts and stops to a taper so the tie-ins fuse. I watch the keyhole and feed rod so the root is full inside. I clean and check the root, then lay fill beads. On the cap I lay stringers from the lower side of the joint up, because the slope makes the metal want to sag. I fill each crater with the downslope.
markingPoints: Reads the WPS and prepares, cleans and lines up the joint
Tacks correctly and tapers the tacks
Fixes the coupon at 45° and does not move it
Welds each half uphill with good tie-ins and a full root
Lays fill and stringer cap beads from the lower side up

essays.stem: Explain what a consumable insert is, when a WPS might call for one, and how a GTAW root is made with it.
essays.modelAnswer: A consumable insert is a ring of filler metal, of a set shape and of a grade that matches the pipe, that is placed in the root of the joint before welding. When the root is welded, the insert is melted fully and becomes part of the weld. A WPS may call for inserts on critical small-bore lines, such as high-pressure or process piping, because they give a smooth, even root inside the pipe, with steady penetration and no drips. The pipe ends are machined to the shape the insert needs. The insert is fitted to one pipe end, the other pipe is brought up tight, and the joint is tacked through the insert. For stainless steel, a back purge is set up first. The root is welded with GTAW, usually with little or no added rod, melting the insert and the pipe edges together. The inside is then checked for full fusion and an even profile.
markingPoints: Defines the insert as a filler ring melted into the root
Gives when it is used (critical lines, even root)
Describes machined ends and fitting the insert
Describes welding the root by fusing the insert, with purge if stainless
Mentions checking the inside profile

essays.stem: Describe how you would make and check a GTAW socket weld on small-bore carbon steel pipe, and explain the gap left at the bottom of the socket.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the WPS for the filler, current and fillet size and the number of passes. I cut the pipe square, remove the burr, and clean the pipe end and the outside of the socket to bright metal. I push the pipe fully into the socket, mark it, then pull it back about 1.5 mm and tack it. The gap lets the pipe grow as it heats, and stops the weld being strained and cracked when the pipe end would otherwise press on the bottom of the socket. I weld the fillet round the joint in at least the number of passes the WPS gives, keeping the legs even on the pipe and the fitting, and filling the craters. I check the gap mark is still showing, then measure the fillet legs with a gauge and look for undercut, overlap and porosity. Where the job asks for it, the welds are checked with dye penetrant or magnetic particle.
markingPoints: Prepares and cleans the pipe and socket
Pulls the pipe back to leave the gap and tacks it
Explains the gap prevents cracking from expansion
Welds even fillet passes to the WPS, filling craters
Checks the gap, leg size and surface faults

essays.stem: Compare manual GTAW and orbital GTAW for butt welding stainless steel tube. Cover the set-up, the person's qualification, the joint preparation and when each is the better choice.
essays.modelAnswer: In manual GTAW the welder holds the torch and feeds the rod, adjusting the heat and speed by eye as he goes round the tube. He must hold a welder qualification for the process, positions and sizes. Joint preparation can allow for small faults in fit-up, because the welder can adjust. In orbital GTAW a weld head clamps onto the tube and turns the tungsten round it by itself, following a program of current, pulse and speed. The person running it is a welding operator, qualified on that machine. The tube ends must be cut square and faced, and lined up very closely, because the machine cannot see or correct poor fit-up. Purging is the same for both. Manual GTAW is better for a few joints, awkward places and repairs. Orbital welding is better for many joints of the same size, such as clean food or pharmaceutical lines, because it gives very even, repeatable welds.
markingPoints: Manual: welder controls heat and rod; welder qualification
Orbital: programmed head; welding operator qualification
Orbital needs square, faced ends and tight fit-up
Purge needed for both on stainless
Says when each is the better choice

essays.stem: Explain how a welder's GTAW pipe qualification limits the work he may do, and how a supervisor checks this before giving him a job.
essays.modelAnswer: A welder's pipe qualification is recorded on his WPQ. Under the AWS code the Centre uses, it is limited by what he did in the test. The diameter range comes from the code's tables for the pipe size tested, so a small pipe test covers larger pipe but a large pipe test may not cover small bore. The wall thickness tested sets the thickness of weld metal he may lay. The position tested sets the positions covered; 6G generally covers most positions. Whether he used backing, an insert or an open root also matters, and so does the filler group. If he used GTAW only for the root, his GTAW deposit thickness is limited to what he laid. The supervisor reads the job's pipe sizes, walls and positions, compares them with the WPQ, and checks the continuity record shows the welder has used GTAW within the time the code allows.
markingPoints: Names the WPQ and that it is limited by the test
Diameter and wall/deposit thickness limits
Position, backing or insert and filler group limits
Compares the job details with the WPQ
Checks continuity is up to date

essays.stem: A radiograph shows lack of fusion in the root of a GTAW pipe weld. Describe the steps to repair it so the client will accept it.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the film report to find the exact place and length of the fault, and mark it on the pipe from the weld number and the film markers. I tell the supervisor, and record the repair on the weld log. I check that there is a repair WPS, or that the original WPS covers the repair. I grind out the faulty area from the outside, with a taper at each end, until I reach sound metal, and check with dye penetrant or by eye that the fault is gone. For stainless steel I set up the purge again. I re-weld the cavity with GTAW to the WPS, by a qualified welder, fusing the ends of the groove well. After the weld cools, it is inspected by eye and X-rayed again at the same place. Only when the new film is accepted is the repair closed out on the records.
markingPoints: Locates the fault from the film and marks it
Records the repair and checks a WPS covers it
Grinds out to sound metal with tapered ends and checks
Re-welds to the WPS, by a qualified welder, with purge if needed
Re-inspects and re-radiographs, then closes the record

essays.stem: Describe the hazards of GTAW pipe welding in a working hotel plant room or factory, and how you would control them.
essays.modelAnswer: The pipes may hold water, steam, fuel or chemicals, so the line must be isolated, locked off, drained and proven safe, with a permit, before work starts. Nearby lines and equipment can catch fire or be damaged, so I clear or cover burnable things, keep an extinguisher close and leave a fire watch after the work. The arc gives off strong ultraviolet light, so I put up screens to protect staff passing by. Argon can collect in low rooms and pits, so the room is ventilated and cylinders are chained upright and shut after use. High-frequency starting can upset computers and controls in the plant, so I warn the plant staff and keep leads short. Hot pipe is marked. Access may be at height or in tight spaces, so a safe platform is used. I follow the plant's rules, the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules.
markingPoints: Isolate, drain and permit the line before work
Fire control: clear, cover, extinguisher and fire watch
UV screens to protect others
Argon build-up and cylinder care
HF interference, hot pipe and access controlled

essays.stem: Many pipe procedures use GTAW for the root and MMAW for the fill and cap. Explain why, how the change-over is made, and what records are kept.
essays.modelAnswer: GTAW gives a clean, smooth, fully fused root with good control of penetration, which is what the inside of a pipe needs. But GTAW lays metal slowly, so filling a thick wall with it would take a long time. MMAW lays metal faster, so it is used for the fill and cap to save time. The WPS gives both processes, the filler for each, and how thick the GTAW layer must be before MMAW starts. Usually a second GTAW pass is laid on the root so the first MMAW pass cannot burn through it. The GTAW passes are cleaned and checked before the change. Electrodes for MMAW, such as low-hydrogen ones, are kept in the oven and quiver. The records show both processes on the PQR and WPS, and each welder's WPQ shows the thickness of weld metal he is qualified to lay with each process.
markingPoints: GTAW root for quality and control
MMAW fill and cap for speed
Enough GTAW thickness before MMAW, to avoid burn-through
Cleaning, checking and electrode care at change-over
Records show both processes and deposit thicknesses

essays.stem: You are to lead the GTAW welding of a small-bore pipe skid with 30 joints for a factory in Spanish Town. Explain how you would plan the job from the drawings to hand-over.
essays.modelAnswer: I study the isometric drawings and number every weld. I list the pipe sizes, walls, materials and positions, and check that there is a WPS for each kind of joint and that every welder's WPQ covers them. I order pipe, fittings, filler, tungstens and argon, and check the mill certificates when they come. I agree hold points with the client's inspector, such as fit-up of the first joints and any X-rays. I plan the order of work so spools are made on the bench in easy positions, leaving only the closing welds in fixed positions. I set up safe bays with extraction, and a purge set if stainless is used. During the job I check fit-ups, settings and visual quality, and fill in the weld log with each weld's welder and date. At the end I make sure all tests are done and passed, the spools are clean and capped, and the records are complete for hand-over.
markingPoints: Studies drawings and numbers welds
Checks WPS and WPQs cover the work; orders and checks materials
Agrees hold points and inspection with the client
Plans the order of work, with most welds in easy positions
Keeps the weld log and completes tests and records at hand-over

essays.stem: Explain why a welded pipe system is often pressure tested with water, and describe how the test is done safely.
essays.modelAnswer: A water (hydrostatic) test proves that the welds and joints hold the pressure the system will see, with a margin, and shows any leaks. Water is used because it hardly compresses, so it stores little energy; if a weld fails, the pressure drops at once instead of blowing apart as compressed air would. Before the test, all welding and inspection must be finished. The system is closed with rated blanks, and parts that must not be tested are isolated. It is filled with clean water from the low point while the air is let out at the high points. The pressure is raised slowly with a test pump to the figure in the specification, read on a calibrated gauge, and held for the set time. People stay clear while the pressure is raised. Then every weld is checked for leaks. The pressure is let off slowly, the water drained, and the result recorded and signed.
markingPoints: States the purpose: prove strength and find leaks
Explains why water is safer than air
Prepares: work finished, blanks, isolation, air vented
Raises pressure slowly to the specified figure on a calibrated gauge and holds it
Keeps people clear, checks welds, drains and records

practical1.title: Carbon steel pipe test coupon welded with GTAW in the 6G position to a WPS, with visual inspection, bend tests and WPQ records
practical1.brief: Your group is given a WPS for a carbon steel pipe butt joint welded with GTAW for all passes. Each member prepares and welds one pipe coupon (two short pieces of small-bore pipe, about 50–75 mm across, as the assessor provides) in the 6G position. If the Centre has fewer 6G stands than members, members take turns and the others prepare coupons and act as witness. Each member bevels or checks the bevels, sets the root face and gap, checks the inside line-up with a hi-lo gauge, tacks, and marks the top of the coupon. Each member then welds the root, fill and cap without moving the coupon. A witness records the real current, gas flow, tungsten and filler on the group's record sheet. After welding, each member inspects another member's coupon by eye, inside and out, and records the result. The assessor chooses coupons for bend tests, which the group marks out from the places the code sets. Each member completes a draft WPQ for his or her own coupon. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Bevelled carbon steel pipe pieces, about 50–75 mm outside diameter, two per member
ER70S-2 filler rods, 1.6 mm and 2.4 mm, in labelled tubes
GTAW sets on DCEN, torches, cups and tungstens, with argon and flowmeters
Hi-lo gauge, bevel gauge, root gap gauge, weld gauge and inspection mirror
Grinder with grinding and thin cutting discs, files, solvent and rags
WPS, witness record sheet and blank WPQ forms (from the assessor)
Saw and guided bend jig (used by the assessor or under direct supervision)
photos: A tacked coupon with the hi-lo gauge in use
A coupon fixed in the 6G stand, with the top marked
A finished root seen from inside with the mirror
Finished caps on every member's coupon, with the coupon numbers showing
Bend strips after bending, labelled by coupon and position
checklist: Prepared and lined up the joint to the WPS and checked it with gauges
Tacked correctly, tapered the tacks and marked the coupon top
Did not move the coupon from 6G during the test
Welded a fully fused root with good tie-ins and even penetration
Laid fill and cap beads with no undercut, overlap or arc strikes
Witnessed another member's test and recorded real values correctly
Inspected a coupon inside and out and completed a draft WPQ
safety: Bolt or clamp the 6G stand firmly before welding; check it at the start
Weld only in screened bays with extraction; wear full welding PPE
Do not touch the pipe with a bare hand while starting the arc with HF
Hot coupons go to the cooling area, marked HOT
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Small-bore pipe assembly with GTAW socket welds and butt welds, built from an isometric, with dye penetrant checks and a weld log
practical2.brief: Your group is given a simple isometric drawing of a small-bore pipe assembly, such as a short run with two socket-weld elbows, a socket-weld tee and one butt joint, and a WPS for each kind of joint. As a group, number every weld on the drawing and share out the work so each member makes at least one socket weld and has a part in the butt joint (fit-up, root, or fill and cap). Work out and cut the pipe lengths, allowing for the socket depth and the 1.5 mm pull-back gap. Each member prepares, fits and GTAW welds his or her own joints, marking the gap before welding. One member keeps the weld log: weld number, welder, date, filler and result. When the assembly is finished, check its sizes against the drawing, inspect every weld by eye and with a fillet gauge, and carry out a dye penetrant check on two welds chosen by the assessor. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Small-bore carbon steel pipe, about 15–25 mm, with socket-weld elbows, a tee and couplings (as the assessor provides)
Short pieces of pipe for the butt joint, bevelled or square as the WPS says
ER70S-2 filler rods, 1.6 mm, in labelled tubes
GTAW sets on DCEN, torches, tungstens and argon with flowmeters
Pipe cutter or saw, deburring tool, files, tape measure and square
Fillet gauge, marker and a dye penetrant kit (cleaner, penetrant, developer) with its SDS
Isometric drawing, WPS sheets and a blank weld log (from the assessor)
photos: The isometric with every weld numbered
A socket joint with the pipe pulled back and the gap marked
Socket welds and the butt joint after welding
